criterion_scores.reasoning: The acceptance-criteria-visible behaviour is correct today: check-refs.sh on substrate.py and identity_probe.py both report 0 missing (verified live), the SessionStart-class false positives are gone, and a fabricated/typo'd name still flags via the artifact-scan path (verified live with a constructed probe file). But the underlying classification rule is file-level co-occurrence, not the name-scoped 'writes THAT ledger' rule decision (1)/(4) specify, and I reproduced by direct execution a case where a read-only reference is wrongly excused — squarely the case decision (1) says must still flag. This is a genuine, demonstrated contradiction of a numbered spec decision, not a hypothetical nitpick, so it caps here regardless of how clean the rest of the code is.

All required parts are present (check-refs.sh integration, shared runtime_ledgers.py module, build_graph.py mirror, three layers of selftest), no TODO stubs, and the acceptance criteria I could check (0 missing on substrate.py/identity_probe.py, typo still flags) all hold. But one of the three selftest layers — the 'unbacked' live-repo guard — is non-functional (tautological, proven by direct execution), which means the specific failure mode this whole change exists to prevent (a name excused without a real per-name writer) has no actual regression coverage, despite being advertised as covered. That's a load-bearing gap in an artifact whose entire purpose is precision about exactly this distinction.

File placement is correct (.claude/hooks/runtime_ledgers.py alongside check-refs.sh, executable bit set like its siblings), naming has no alex: prefix issue (not a skill), no MCP/Notion writes involved, no subagent-fan-out concerns. ADR-8 D2's single-shared-rule requirement is honored properly — both check-refs.sh and build_graph.py import/call the same runtime_ledgers.py rather than keeping two copies in sync by comment. One cosmetic nit: the cross-directory sys.path import in build_graph.py is a bit fragile plumbing, though it's the correct architectural response to ADR-8 D2.

The fix is appropriately scoped — no speculative surface, no duplicated state beyond what ADR-8 D2 requires, no resurrected tombstoned decision, no hardcoded secrets, no fabricated numbers. But the vacuous 'unbacked' guard is itself a mild instance of test theater: code presented as a verification step that structurally cannot fail is the same failure class (false rigor/false assurance) that this whole judge-and-gate layer exists to catch, and it sits right next to genuinely good negative-control tests in the same function, making it easy to mistake for real coverage.

Most of this diff is unusually transparent: the KNOWN LIMITATION section honestly discloses the file-level co-occurrence approximation and even names the exact failure mode I reproduced ('a file that appends to ledger A and only READS ledger B would excuse a missing B'), the SCOPE section states its own boundary, and the check-refs.sh stderr message clearly reports the runtime-ledger skip count. That transparency is real credit. But the SELF-EXCLUSION docstring's claim that the selftest verifies names are 'backed... not only that the positives are present' overstates what the code actually checks (see completeness/anti-pattern defects) — an unverified property stated as verified, which is the specific diagnostics fail-anchor pattern.

defects.quote: +  3. that same file performs an append-mode write (`open(..., "a"…)` / `open(..., mode="a"…)` / `>>`).
defects.issue: RULE condition 3 (and its implementation in ledgers_from_texts/APPEND_RE.search(text)) tests whether the FILE contains any append call anywhere, not whether THAT LEDGER's own write is append-mode. I verified by direct execution: given one file with a real append to ledger A and a separate, never-appended, read-only reference to ledger B, is_runtime_ledger(B) returns True. This contradicts YED-227 decision (1) — 'some tracked script in the repo writes THAT LEDGER only in append mode... a ledger that is only ever read' should still flag — and decision (4)'s 'read-only reference to a missing file still flags' selftest requirement, which is only tested for a file with zero append calls at all (the 'reader.py' fixture), never for the mixed-file case. The KNOWN LIMITATION note (lines 304-308) discloses this candidly but discloses it as acceptable rather than fixing it, and it is currently dormant only because every co-located name in the live repo happens to also have its own genuine writer — the mechanism itself is not name-scoped.
defects.decision: spec-drift; correctness capped ≤0.70 per rubric (behaviour contradicts numbered decisions 1 and 4)

defects.quote: +    unbacked = sorted(n for n in live if not any(n in t for t in writers.values()))
defects.issue: This is presented (in the comment above it and in the SELF-EXCLUSION docstring) as a live-repo guard proving 'every live name must be backed by a writer file.' It cannot fail: `live` names are derived from `ledgers_from_texts(writers)` via regex extraction FROM those same texts, so `n in t` is tautologically true for the very `t` it came from. I confirmed this by re-running the check against my own adversarial fixture (ledger B, with no real append writer for its own name) — `unbacked` still came back empty. The one case this test exists to catch (defect above) is exactly the case it cannot catch. Test coverage for the mixed-file/co-occurrence risk is silently absent despite being advertised as covered.
defects.decision: fix-required — either make this check dataflow-aware (verify the SPECIFIC name is appended, not just present in a file that appends something) or drop the claim that it verifies 'backed'

defects.quote: +asserts the negative controls are ABSENT from the live set, not only that the positives are present.
defects.issue: This docstring line asserts the selftest now verifies both that negative controls are absent (true, and non-tautological) AND that positives are correctly present/backed (the 'unbacked' check) — but as shown above, the 'backed' half of that claim is vacuous by construction. The comment overstates what was actually proven, which is the same shape of issue (a claimed property the code doesn't actually have) that the diagnostics fail-anchor calls out.
defects.decision: advisory — tighten the docstring to describe only what the guard can actually detect, or fix the guard to match the claim

defects.issue: build_graph.py (.claude/scripts/) reaches across into .claude/hooks/ via sys.path manipulation to import runtime_ledgers as a bare module. This is exactly what ADR-8 D2 asks for (one shared rule, not two copies), so it's the right call architecturally, but the relative-path plumbing is a bit fragile (breaks if build_graph.py is ever invoked from a copied/relocated location rather than its real path) and there's no fallback/error message if the import fails.
defects.decision: note-only — acceptable given ADR-8 D2, not a blocker
